question: Why does your phone screen get smudged even when you never touch it?
why_curious: We all marvel at how clean our phones can look after a quick wipe, yet almost immediately fingerprints and smudges appear as if by magic. The culprit is not just dirt or sweat but a microscopic oleophobic coating that wears away with everyday use, allowing oils from our skin to seep through and cling to the glass. It’s a hidden battle between surface chemistry and our daily habits that keeps our screens looking dirty despite our best efforts.
curiosity_gap: People think smudges happen only when we touch the screen, but in reality they can appear without any contact, driven by the gradual breakdown of the protective film.
